title: Rusk's Room above the Fishstairs — Sill
caption: The old man's room above the Fishstairs and below the north bridge, drawn close at the scale of a hand laid on a drawer: the floorboards and their cold, the locked drawer with its small lock left shut, a bench and the stool nobody sees him use, the pot he taps for its note, the ice-mouse-fur coat and salt-stiff hat on their pegs, and the ash in the corners unswept; the window over the steps, the stair down, the four Fishstairs steps and the out-of-line landing where a fifth should stand, the bridge over the Ilm with the fish-trade shade beneath it, the Singing Sill and its four-foot fall, the river road upriver to the Weir and the Eel House and downriver to Greybank, with the Cross and its moot-post and Slate Row drawn faint at the edges. Cartouche dated Y.H. 813, the month of Ash, with compass, a hundred-pace scale, a convention of signs and surveyor's notes on the man who never sits down indoors and turns a question back on the asker, the paper read once a year on the Last Day that no surveyor has set down, and the boy who turned his head toward a pot before anybody tapped it. An engraved key with its small ward sits in the margin.
